scenes.headline: How Kimi K3.1 Pro improved on Kimi K3
scenes.sub: The same experts, a new attention indexer, much more reinforcement learning.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Bowline! Kimi K3.1 Pro is Moonshot's new flagship. The launch said: same model, more training. The weights say a little more.

scenes.title: What carried over from K3
scenes.sub: Read from every safetensors header, no weights downloaded
scenes.say: Chapter one. What carried over from K3.

steps.term: KDA: Kimi Delta Attention, a linear-attention layer
steps.say: K3's architecture. Ninety-three layers, mostly Kimi Delta Attention, a linear attention with a constant-size state. Every fourth is a full-attention Gated MLA layer.
Every layer feeds a mixture of experts. Each token goes to sixteen of eight hundred and ninety-six.
The article read the header of all ninety-six weight shards in both repositories. K3 has four hundred ninety-seven thousand tensors.
Every one is in K3.1 Pro, same name, same shape, same precision. But no shard's hash matches, so the weights moved everywhere.
And there are a hundred and twenty new tensors, five in each of twenty-four layers.
About a hundred and seventy-nine million new parameters. Exactly the gap between the two models' counts.

scenes.title: A sparse-attention indexer
scenes.sub: Gated MLA gains a scout in front of it

scenes.label: What's new
scenes.text: Each full-attention layer gains a small indexer that scores every earlier token and passes only the top 2,048 to attention.
scenes.say: The twenty-four new sets of tensors sit in the twenty-four full-attention layers. Each is a small indexer that scores every earlier token and passes only the best two thousand and forty-eight to attention.

steps.say: Open one of those layers. The tensor names are DeepSeek's lightning indexer, and the model card calls the layer Gated DSA.

steps.term: Indexer: scores which tokens attention reads
steps.say: Reading from the shapes: the indexer forms thirty-two small query heads from the query latent the layer already computes.
It scores every earlier token, using one small key per token. No positional encoding.
Only the top two thousand and forty-eight reach the real attention. Below that much context, nothing is left out.

steps.note: no modelling code ships: the mechanism is read from tensor names
steps.say: The repository ships no modelling code, so this is the article's reading of the tensors, not something run.

legend: K3.1 Pro: score every token, cheaply
The price: 22% more cache in those layers

steps.say: In K3, each full-attention layer reads every earlier token. Those twenty-four layers are the only part whose cost grows with context.
In K3.1 Pro, the indexer scores every earlier token first, with one small key each, a hundred and twenty-eight wide.
Only the top two thousand and forty-eight reach the real attention. Below that much context, nothing is left out.
At the full million-token window, the expensive attention reads five hundred and twelve times fewer entries. The indexer still scans everything, but cheaply.
The price: if the indexer key is cached too, those layers store twenty-two percent more per token.

items: Joint RL across hundreds of domains
right.say: K3.1 Pro runs joint reinforcement learning across hundreds of domains, and strips cyber data, even from mid-training.

steps.say: Start from the K3 checkpoint. The experts keep their shape.
Most of the cost is generation: long agent runs against tools, in sandboxes across hundreds of domains.
Every domain has its own reward. One buggy environment can teach the wrong thing, so Moonshot vets them on a shared platform.
Then update, and around again. The claim is that extra compute now pays off predictably.

items.say: Against the proprietary models, K3.1 Pro is ahead or tied on sixteen of forty-five rows, mostly agentic ones.
Counted per response, the hallucination drop is fifty-seven point six percent.
And a viral demo's tokens and price cannot both be right at Moonshot's own rates.
